Open the Wizard Product Updates Darwin & Sensitivity Labels Enforcement: Your Purview Classifications, Enforced Beyond Microsoft Read the post Product Updates Darwin & Notification Center: Governance Signal, Delivered to the Right People at the Right Time Read the post Latest Darwin & Sensitivity Labels Enforcement Darwin & Notification Center Procurement Pricing Contract Vehicles Cooperative State Federal Company About Us Partnerships News & Press Careers Contact Contact Us Book a Demo Darwin's Sensitivity Labels Enforcement: Your Purview Classifications, Enforced Beyond Microsoft Most agencies have already done the work: files classified in Microsoft Purview, labels embedded into every document, policy decisions built into the data itself. Inside Microsoft, those labels work. Outside Microsoft, they stop mattering. A Confidential file uploads to ChatGPT as easily as a public one. Darwin's Sensitivity Labels Enforcement changes that. m August 5, 2026 by Darwin AI Most agencies have already done the hard work of classifying their data. Files marked Confidential. Documents labeled Special Handling. Records tagged Public Information. Every one of those labels represents a policy decision; this data can be shared this way, this data can't, embedded directly into the file through Microsoft Purview. That classification works exactly as designed inside the Microsoft ecosystem. Open a Confidential document in Word, share it in SharePoint, send it through Teams: the label controls what happens. But the moment an employee drags that same file into ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude, the label stops mattering. Every classification decision the agency has made is invisible to the AI tool receiving the file. This is the gap Darwin's Sensitivity Labels Enforcement closes. Darwin reads the Purview label already embedded in every file and enforces the agency's classification policy at the moment of upload; across ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, and Microsoft 365 Copilot Cloud. The classification investment that used to stop at the Microsoft boundary now protects data everywhere employees work with AI. File upload rules—configure enforcement by sensitivity label, per AI tool category, in one place. The Classification You've Already Built, Now Working for AI Sensitivity Labels Enforcement doesn't ask agencies to reclassify anything. Darwin syncs sensitivity labels directly from Microsoft Purview through the existing Entra integration, using the standard Graph API permission for label access. Every label the agency has already defined in Purview- Public Information, Confidential, Confidential-Special Handling, and any custom labels in between is available in Darwin the moment sync completes. When an employee uploads a file to an AI tool, Darwin reads the label embedded in the file itself and enforces the rule in real time. No re-tagging. No parallel classification system. No new workflow for the data governance team. The years already invested in Purview classification become AI policy on day one. Three Modes of Enforcement, Configured Per AI Tool Category Agencies don't want the same level of enforcement everywhere. A shadow AI tool discovered in an employee's browser demands stricter controls than a sandboxed tool the security team is actively evaluating. Sensitivity Labels Enforcement supports that reality with three configurable enforcement modes: Block all files — the strictest option, preventing any file upload regardless of label Block only labeled files (deny-list) — block specific sensitivity levels while allowing everything else, ideal for keeping Confidential and above out of unauthorized AI tools Allow only labeled files (allow-list) — permit only files with explicitly approved labels, blocking everything else including unlabeled files Each rule is configured per AI system category: unauthorized, authorized, sandboxed, or shadow so agencies can enforce strict blocking on the tools that need it while allowing more flexibility where risk is lower. It's granular control, not the blunt on/off switch that pushes employees toward shadow AI. Every Enforcement Action, Visible and Auditable When Darwin blocks a file upload, the action doesn't disappear into a log no one checks. Every violation raises an alert in the Risk Center with full context: which user, which tool, which file, which label ready for investigation. Users who need to upload a legitimately blocked file can request an exception, giving them a sanctioned path instead of a workaround. The result is enforcement that compliance teams can actually audit and defend. Not a policy that lives in a training document, but one that operates in real time and produces a record every time it fires. Built for the Way Security Teams Actually Work Government and regulated agencies have invested years in building classification schemes that reflect their compliance obligations. Open the Wizard Product Updates Darwin & Sensitivity Labels Enforcement: Your Purview Classifications, Enforced Beyond Microsoft Read the post Product Updates Darwin & Notification Center: Governance Signal, Delivered to the Right People at the Right Time Read the post Latest Darwin & Sensitivity Labels Enforcement Darwin & Notification Center Procurement Pricing Contract Vehicles Cooperative State Federal Company About Us Partnerships News & Press Careers Contact Contact Us Book a Demo Darwin's Notification Center: Governance Signal, Delivered to the Right People at the Right Time Every day, governance teams miss events that need a fast response. Not because Darwin isn't catching them, but because catching them has meant logging into the platform to check. A critical alert sits unseen. An access request waits days for a decision. A newly discovered shadow AI tool operates for a week before the right person notices. Darwin's Notification Center changes that. m July 30, 2026 by Darwin AI Across state and local government, AI governance runs on signal. New tools appearing across AI governance. New tools appearing across departments. Shadow AI sessions surfacing. Risk levels shifting on tools already in use. Alerts firing on PII, prompt injection, or access requests waiting on a decision. Every one of these events matters, and every one requires someone to act on it quickly. The problem for most governance teams isn't that the signal doesn't exist. It's that catching it has meant logging into the platform, opening each area, and checking manually. A critical alert can sit unseen until someone happens to check. An access request can wait days for a decision. A newly discovered shadow AI tool can operate for a week before the right person notices. Darwin's Notification Center closes that gap. Admins and users can now choose exactly which governance events trigger an email, how often those emails arrive, and who receives them, so time-sensitive signal reaches the right people the moment it matters. Organization Notifications—route governance events to shared inboxes, distribution lists, or team mailboxes, with per-category and per-severity control. Two Levels of Notifications, One Coherent System Notification Center works at two levels that mirror how governance teams actually operate. Organization Notifications lets admins set a shared list of recipient email addresses, a distribution list, a monitoring mailbox, a team inbox, and control which organization-wide events route to it. My Notifications lets each user configure the same categories for their own account, tuned to their focus and role. Both levels draw from the same set of categories: new AI tools discovered (manually added or detected as shadow AI), Risk Center alerts across every severity level, patch version updates, and access requests including rule overrides and evidence review. The result is one coherent notification system that supports both team-wide routing and individual preferences without conflict. My Notifications—every user tunes the same categories for their own account, matched to their role and focus. Signal Volume You Actually Control Governance events aren't all equally urgent, and Notification Center gives teams the controls to reflect that. Every category can be turned on or off independently, so admins subscribe to exactly the events that matter to their role, no more, no less. Risk Center alerts can be filtered further by severity, from Critical down to Low, so teams choose the noise floor that matches their capacity. Delivery frequency is equally flexible. Choose Immediate to receive an email the moment an event fires, ideal for time-sensitive alerts and access requests. Or choose Aggregated to receive a single email that groups related notifications by area, perfect for teams that want awareness without a full inbox. The outcome: signal over noise, tuned to how each person and each team actually works. Route Governance to the Right Place For many agencies, governance isn't a one-person job. Shadow AI discoveries need to reach the IT team. Access requests need to reach the compliance officer. Risk analysis changes need to reach the security lead. Notification Center supports that reality by letting admins route Organization Notifications to shared inboxes, distribution lists, or system monitoring accounts, wherever the response actually happens. Where multiple admins share coverage, each can subscribe to different categories in My Notifications, splitting responsibility without missing events. The team stays aligned on AI oversight, and each person receives only what's relevant to them. Built for the Way Governance Teams Actually Work State and local government agencies are being asked to demonstrate active AI oversight, not just that policies exist, but that events are seen, decisions are made, and responses happen fast. Darwin's Notification Center gives governance, security, and compliance teams the awareness infrastructure to do exactly that, without depending on anyone remembering to log in and check.
